name: airport_connections
title: Connections Among U.S. Airports Interactive
description:
This example shows all the connections between major U.S. airports. Lookup transformations
are used to find the coordinates of each airport and connecting airports. Connections
are displayed on pointerover via a single selection.

name: anscombe_plot
title: Anscombe's Quartet
description:
`Anscombe's Quartet <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anscombe%27s_quartet>`_
is a famous dataset constructed by Francis Anscombe.
It is made of 4 different subsets of data.
Each subset has very different characteristics, even though common summary
statistics such as mean and variance are identical.

This example shows how to make a faceted plot, with each facet
showing a different subset of the data.

name: area_chart_gradient
title: Area Chart with Gradient
description:
This example shows how to make an area chart with a gradient fill.
For more information about gradient options see the Vega-Lite `Gradient documentation <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/docs/types.html#gradient>`_.

name: area_faceted
title: Faceted Area Chart
description:
Multiple area subcharts, one for each company.
We also show filtering out one of the companies,
and sorting the companies in a custom order.

name: bar_and_line_with_dual_axis
title: Bar Chart with Line on Dual Axis
description:
This example shows how to combine two plots and keep their axes.

For a more polished version of this chart, see :ref:`gallery_wheat_wages`.

name: bar_chart_faceted_compact
title: Compact Faceted Grid of Bar Charts
description:
A simple grid of bar charts to compare performance data,
one subchart for each subset of the data.

name: bar_chart_horizontal
title: Horizontal Bar Chart
description: This example is a bar chart drawn horizontally by putting the quantitative value on the x axis.

name: bar_chart_sorted
title: Sorted Bar Chart
description: This example shows a bar chart sorted by a calculated value.

name: bar_chart_with_highlighted_bar
title: Bar Chart with Highlighted Bar
description: This example shows a basic bar chart with a single bar highlighted.

name: bar_chart_with_highlighted_segment
title: Bar Chart with Highlighted Segment
description: This example shows a bar chart that highlights values beyond a threshold.

name: bar_chart_with_labels
title: Bar Chart with Labels
description: This example shows a basic horizontal bar chart with labels created with Altair.

name: bar_chart_with_labels_measured_luminance
title: Bar Chart with Labels based on Measured Luminance
description: This example shows a basic horizontal bar chart with labels where the measured luminance to decides if the text overlay is be colored ``black`` or ``white``.

name: bar_chart_with_mean_line
title: Bar Chart with Line at Mean
description: This example shows the mean value overlaid on a bar chart.

name: bar_chart_with_negatives
title: Bar Chart with Negative Values
description: This example shows a bar chart with both positive and negative values.

name: bar_chart_with_range
title: Bar Chart with Range
description: This example shows a range bar chart where each bar displays information of a low and high value.

name: bar_chart_with_single_threshold
title: Bar Chart Highlighting Values beyond a Threshold
description: This example shows a bar chart highlighting values beyond a threshold.

name: bar_faceted_stacked
title: Faceted Stacked Bar Chart
description:
A horizontal stacked bar chart using barley crop yield data.
The chart is horizontally faceted based on the year,
and vertically faceted based on variety.

name: bar_rounded
title: Bar Chart with Rounded Edges
description: This example shows how to create a bar chart with rounded edges.

name: bar_with_rolling_mean
title: Bar Chart with Rolling Mean
description: A bar chart overlaid with a rolling mean. In this example the average of values over the previous decade is displayed as a line.

name: beckers_barley_facet
title: Becker's Barley Faceted Plot
description:
The example demonstrates the faceted charts created by Richard Becker,
William Cleveland and others in the 1990s. Using the visualization technique
where each row is a different site (i.e. the chart is faceted by site),
they identified an anomaly in a widely used agriculatural dataset,
where the "Morris" site accidentally had the years 1931 and 1932 swapped.
They named this
`"The Morris Mistake." <http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/stat695t/writings/Trellis.User.pdf>`_.

name: beckers_barley_wrapped_facet
title: Becker's Barley Wrapped Facet Plot
description:
The example demonstrates the faceted charts created by Richard Becker,
William Cleveland and others in the 1990s. Using the visualization technique
where each row is a different site (i.e. the chart is faceted by site),
they identified an anomaly in a widely used agriculatural dataset,
where the "Morris" site accidentally had the years 1931 and 1932 swapped.
They named this
`"The Morris Mistake." <http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/stat695t/writings/Trellis.User.pdf>`_.

name: boxplot
title: Boxplot with Min/Max Whiskers
description:
This example shows how to make a boxplot using US Population data from 2000.
Note that the default value of the `extent` property is 1.5,
which represents the convention of extending the whiskers
to the furthest points within 1.5 * IQR from the first and third quartile.

name: bubble_plot
title: Bubble Plot
description: This example shows how to make a bubble plot.

name: bump_chart
title: Bump Chart
description:
This example shows a bump chart.  The data is first grouped into six-month
intervals using pandas. The ranks are computed by Altair using a
window transform.

name: calculate_residuals
title: Calculate Residuals
description:
A dot plot showing each movie in the database, and the difference from the average movie rating.
The display is sorted by year to visualize everything in sequential order.
The graph is for all Movies before 2019.

Adapted from `Calculate Residuals <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/joinaggregate_residual_graph.html>`_.

name: candlestick_chart
title: Candlestick Chart
description:
A candlestick chart inspired from `Protovis <http://mbostock.github.io/protovis/ex/candlestick.html>`_.
This example shows the performance of the Chicago Board Options Exchange `Volatility Index <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VIX>`_ (VIX)
in the summer of 2009. The thick bar represents the opening and closing prices,
while the thin bar shows intraday high and low prices; if the index closed higher on a given day, the bars are colored green rather than red.

name: choropleth
title: Choropleth Map
description: A choropleth map of unemployment rate per county in the US

name: choropleth_repeat
title: Repeated Choropleth Map
description: Three choropleths representing disjoint data from the same table.

name: co2_concentration
title: Atmospheric CO2 Concentration
description:
This example is a fully developed line chart that uses a window transformation.
It was inspired by `Gregor Aisch's work at datawrapper
<https://www.datawrapper.de/_/OHgEm/>`_.

name: comet_chart
title: Comet Chart
description:
Inspired by `Zan Armstrong's comet chart <https://www.zanarmstrong.com/infovisresearch>`_
this plot uses ``mark_trail`` to visualize change of grouped data over time.
A more elaborate example and explanation of creating comet charts in Altair
is shown in `this blogpost <https://medium.com/de-dataverbinders/comet-charts-in-python-visualizing-statistical-mix-effects-and-simpsons-paradox-with-altair-6cd51fb58b7c>`_.

name: cumulative_count_chart
title: Cumulative Count Chart
description:
This example shows an area chart with cumulative count.
Adapted from https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/area_cumulative_freq.html

name: dendrogram
title: Dendrogram of Hierarchical Clustering
description:
This is a dendrogram from the result of a hierarchical clustering. It's based on the example from
https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/cluster/plot_agglomerative_dendrogram.html

name: density_repeat
title: Repeated Density Estimates
description:
Density estimates for each measurement of penguins.
This is what we call a "repeated" plot, with one subplot
for each measurement type. All measurements are in millimeters,
making them directly comparable on a shared x-axis.

name: density_stack
title: Stacked Density Estimates
description:
To plot a stacked graph of estimates, use a shared ``extent`` and a fixed
number of subdivision ``steps`` to ensure that the points for each area align
well.  Density estimates of body mass for each penguin species are plotted
in a stacked method.  In addition, setting ``counts`` to true multiplies the
densities by the number of data points in each group, preserving proportional
differences.

name: deviation_ellipses
title: Confidence Interval Ellipses
description:
This example shows bivariate deviation ellipses of flipper length and body mass of three penguin species.

Inspired by `ggplot2.stat_ellipse`_ and directly based on `Deviation ellipses example`_ by `@essicolo`_

.. _ggplot2.stat_ellipse:
    https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/stat_ellipse.html#ref-examples
.. _Deviation ellipses example:
    https://github.com/vega/altair/pull/514
.. _@essicolo:
    https://github.com/essicolo

name: distributions_and_medians_of_likert_scale_ratings
title: Distributions and Medians of Likert Scale Ratings
description:
Distributions and Medians of Likert Scale Ratings. (Figure 9 from @jhoffswell and @zcliu’s ‘Interactive Repair of Tables Extracted from PDF Documents on Mobile Devices’ – http://idl.cs.washington.edu/files/2019-InteractiveTableRepair-CHI.pdf).

Adapted from `Distributions and Medians of Likert Scale Ratings <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/layer_likert.html>`_.

name: distributions_faceted_histogram
title: Faceted Histogram
description:
This example shows how to make a basic faceted histogram,
with one histogram subplot for different subsets of the data.

Based off the vega-lite example:
https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/trellis_bar_histogram.html

name: diverging_stacked_bar_chart
title: Diverging Stacked Bar Chart
description: This example shows a diverging stacked bar chart for sentiments towards a set of eight questions, displayed as percentages with neutral responses straddling the 0% mark.

name: donut_chart
title: Donut Chart
description:
This example shows how to make a Donut Chart using ``mark_arc``.
This is adapted from a corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Donut Chart <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/arc_donut.html>`_.

name: dot_dash_plot
title: Dot Dash Plot
description:
How to make the dot-dash plot presented in Edward Tufte's `Visual Display of Quantitative Information <https://www.edwardtufte.com/tufte/books_vdqi>`_. Based
on a JavaScript implementation by `g3o2 <https://bl.ocks.org/g3o2/bd4362574137061c243a2994ba648fb8>`_.

name: empirical_cumulative_distribution_function
title: Empirical Cumulative Distribution Function
description: This example shows an empirical cumulative distribution function.

name: errorbars_with_ci
title: Error Bars with Confidence Interval
description:
This example shows how to show error bars using confidence intervals.
The confidence intervals are computed internally in vega by a non-parametric
`bootstrap of the mean <https://github.com/vega/vega-statistics/blob/master/src/bootstrapCI.js>`_.

name: errorbars_with_std
title: Error Bars with Standard Deviation
description:
This example shows how to show error bars with standard deviation using crop yields data of different
in the years of 1930s.

name: falkensee
title: Population of Falkensee from 1875 to 2014
description: This example is a reproduction of the Falkensee plot found in the Vega-Lite examples.

name: filled_step_chart
title: Filled Step Chart
description: This example shows Google's stock price over time as a step chart with its area filled in and its line emphasized.

name: gantt_chart
title: Gantt Chart
description: This example shows how to make a simple Gantt chart.

name: gapminder_bubble_plot
title: Gapminder Bubble Plot
description:
This example shows how to make a bubble plot showing the correlation between
health and income for 187 countries in the world (modified from an example
in Lisa Charlotte Rost's blog post `'One Chart, Twelve Charting Libraries' <http://lisacharlotterost.github.io/2016/05/17/one-chart-code/>`_.

name: groupby-map
title: Grouped Points with Proportional Symbols Map
description: This is a layered geographic visualization that groups points by state.

name: grouped_bar_chart
title: Grouped Bar Chart
description: This example shows a grouped bar chart.

name: grouped_bar_chart2
title: Grouped Bar Chart with xOffset
description:
Like :ref:`gallery_grouped_bar_chart`, this example shows a grouped bar chart.  Whereas :ref:`gallery_grouped_bar_chart` used the ``column`` encoding channel, this example uses the ``xOffset`` encoding channel.  This is adapted from a corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Grouped Bar Chart <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/bar_grouped.html>`_.

name: grouped_bar_chart_horizontal
title: Horizontal Grouped Bar Chart
description: This example shows a horizontal grouped bar chart.

name: grouped_bar_chart_overlapping_bars
title: Grouped Bar Chart with xOffset and overlapping bars
description: Like :ref:`gallery_grouped_bar_chart2`, this example shows a grouped bar chart using the ``xOffset`` encoding channel, but in this example the bars are partly overlapping within each group.

name: grouped_bar_chart_with_error_bars
title: Grouped Bar Chart with Error Bars
description: This example shows a grouped bar chart with error bars.

name: heat_lane
title: Heat Lane Chart
description: This example shows how to make an alternative form of a histogram `designed at Google <https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2022/07/accessibility-first-approach-chart-visual-design/>`_ with the goal of increasing accessibility.

name: hexbins
title: Hexbin Chart
description: This example shows a hexbin chart.

name: histogram_gradient_color
title: Histogram with Gradient Color
description:
This example shows how to make a histogram with gradient color.
The low-high IMDB rating is represented with the color scheme `pinkyellowgreen`.

name: histogram_heatmap
title: 2D Histogram Heatmap
description: This example shows how to make a heatmap from binned quantitative data.

name: histogram_responsive
title: Histogram with Responsive Bins
description:
This shows an example of a histogram with bins that are responsive to a
selection domain. Click and drag on the bottom panel to see the bins
change on the top panel.

name: histogram_scatterplot
title: 2D Histogram Scatter Plot
description: This example shows how to make a 2d histogram scatter plot.

name: histogram_with_a_global_mean_overlay
title: Histogram with a Global Mean Overlay
description: This example shows a histogram with a global mean overlay.

name: horizon_graph
title: Horizon Graph
description: This example shows how to make a Horizon Graph with 2 layers. (See https://idl.cs.washington.edu/papers/horizon/ for more details on Horizon Graphs.)

name: horizontal_stacked_bar_chart
title: Horizontal Stacked Bar Chart
description: This is an example of a horizontal stacked bar chart using data which contains crop yields over different regions and different years in the 1930s.

name: interactive_aggregation
title: Interactive Chart with Aggregation
description:
This example shows an interactive chart where the range binder controls a
threshold as rule where the datapoints on the left-side are aggregated and on the
right-side are drawn as is.
The ability to slide back and fourth may help you understand how the visualization
represents the aggregation. Adapted from an example by @dwootton.

name: interactive_bar_select_highlight
title: Bar Chart with Highlighting on Hover and Selection on Click
description:
This example shows a bar chart with highlighting on hover and selecting on click. (Inspired by Tableau's interaction style.)

Based on https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/interactive_bar_select_highlight.html

name: interactive_brush
title: Interactive Rectangular Brush
description:
This example shows how to add a simple rectangular brush to a scatter plot.
By clicking and dragging on the plot, you can highlight points within the
range.

name: interactive_column_selection
title: Interactive Selection of Columns
description:
This example shows how columns can be selected interactively
by accessing the values from selector widgets,
and then compute the difference of the selected columns.
It also illustrates how to use `indexof` to filter
columns based on active selection values.

name: interactive_cross_highlight
title: Interactive Chart with Cross-Highlight
description:
This example shows an interactive chart where selections in one portion of
the chart affect what is shown in other panels. Click on the bar chart to
see a detail of the distribution in the upper panel.

name: interactive_layered_crossfilter
title: Interactive Crossfilter
description:
This example shows a multi-panel view of the same data, where you can interactively
select a portion of the data in any of the panels to highlight that portion in any
of the other panels.

name: interactive_legend
title: Interactive Legend
description:
The following shows how to create a chart with an interactive legend, by
binding the selection to ``"legend"``. Such a binding only works with
``selection_point`` when projected over a single field or encoding.

name: interactive_reorder_stacked_bars
title: Reorder stacked bar segments
description:
This example uses a calculate transform
to check the values of the "site" column
vs the clicked values in the legend,
and assigns a lower order (0)
if there is a match.
The use of "indexOf" checks for equality in an array,
which here allows for multiple segments to be reordered
by holding down the shift key while clicking the legend.

name: interactive_scatter_plot
title: Simple Interactive Colored Scatter Plot
description: This example shows how to make an interactive scatter plot.

name: interval_selection
title: Interval Selection with Initial Date Range
description:
This is an example of creating a stacked chart for which the domain of the
top chart can be selected by interacting with the bottom chart. The initial
selection range is set using Python's native datetime objects.

name: interval_selection_map_quakes
title: Interval Selection on a Map
description:
This is an example of a binned bar chart on the right where the filtered overlay
is adjusted by interacting with the map on the left.

name: iowa_electricity
title: Iowa's Renewable Energy Boom
description: This example is a fully developed stacked chart using the sample dataset of Iowa's electricity sources.

name: isotype
title: Isotype Visualization
description:
Isotype Visualization shows the distribution of animals across UK and US.
Inspired by `Only An Ocean Between, 1943 <http://www.thomwhite.co.uk/?p=1303>`_. Population Live Stock, p.13.
This is adapted from Vega-Lite example https://vega.github.io/editor/#/examples/vega-lite/isotype_bar_chart

name: isotype_emoji
title: Isotype Visualization with Emoji
description:
Isotype Visualization shows the distribution of animals across UK and US, using unicode emoji
marks rather than custom SVG paths (see https://altair-viz.github.io/gallery/isotype.html).
This is adapted from Vega-Lite example https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/isotype_bar_chart_emoji.html.

name: isotype_grid
title: Isotype Grid
description: This example is a grid of isotype figures.

name: layer_line_color_rule
title: Line Chart with Layered Aggregates
description:
This example shows how to make a multi-series line chart of the daily closing
stock prices for AAPL, AMZN, GOOG, IBM, and MSFT between 2000 and 2010, along
with a layered rule showing the average values.

name: layered_area_chart
title: Layered Area Chart
description: This example shows a layered area chart.

name: layered_bar_chart
title: Layered Bar Chart
description: This example shows a segmented bar chart that is layered rather than stacked.

name: layered_chart_bar_mark
title: Bar and Tick Chart
description: How to layer a tick chart on top of a bar chart.

name: layered_chart_with_dual_axis
title: Layered chart with Dual-Axis
description: This example shows how to create a second independent y axis.

name: layered_heatmap_text
title: Text over a Heatmap
description: An example of a layered chart of text over a heatmap using the cars dataset.

name: layered_histogram
title: Layered Histogram
description: This example shows how to use opacity to make a layered histogram in Altair.

name: line_chart_with_arrows
title: Line Chart with Arrows
description:
This example shows a simple line chart with two types of arrow annotations.
The Unicode character approach is simpler,
while the line plus triangle :ref:`point mark <user-guide-point-marks>` allows for greater flexibility,
such as customizable arrowheads.

name: line_chart_with_color_datum
title: Line Chart with Datum for Color
description:
An example of using ``datum`` and ``repeat`` to color a multi-series line chart.
This is adapted from this corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Repeat and Layer to Show Different Movie Measures <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/repeat_layer.html>`_.

name: line_chart_with_cumsum
title: Line Chart with Cumulative Sum
description: This chart creates a simple line chart from the cumulative sum of a fields.

name: line_chart_with_cumsum_faceted
title: Faceted Line Chart with Cumulative Sum
description:
This chart creates one facet per natural disaster and shows the cumulative number of deaths for that category.
Note the use of different predicates to filter based on both a list and a range.

name: line_chart_with_custom_legend
title: Line Chart with Custom Legend
description:
This example uses the argmax aggregation function in order to create a custom
legend for a line chart.

name: line_chart_with_datum
title: Line Chart with Datum
description:
An example of using ``datum`` to highlight certain values, including a ``DateTime`` value.
This is adapted from two corresponding Vega-Lite Examples:
`Highlight a Specific Value <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/docs/datum.html#highlight-a-specific-data-value>`_.

name: line_chart_with_generator
title: Line Chart with Sequence Generator
description: This examples shows how to create multiple lines using the sequence generator.

name: line_chart_with_interpolation
title: Line Chart with Interpolation
description: This chart shows a line chart with the path interpolated. A full list of interpolation methods is available `in the documentation <https://altair-viz.github.io/user_guide/generated/core/altair.LineConfig.html?highlight=interpolate#altair-lineconfig>`_.

name: line_chart_with_points
title: Line Chart with Point Markers
description: This chart shows a simple line chart with points marking each value.

name: line_chart_with_points_stroked
title: Line Chart with Stroked Point Markers
description: This example shows a simple line chart with points in a different color.

name: line_custom_order
title: Line Chart with Custom Order
description:
By default, the line's path (order of points in the line) is
determined by data values on the temporal/ordinal field.
However, a field can be mapped to the order channel for a custom path.

For example, to show a pattern of data change over time between
gasoline price and average miles driven per capita we use
order channel to sort the points in the line by time field (year).
The earliest year (1956) is one endpoint and the latest year (2010)
is the other endpoint.

This is based on Hannah Fairfield's article 'Driving Shifts Into Reverse'.
See https://archive.nytimes.com/www.nytimes.com/imagepages/2010/05/02/business/02metrics.html.

name: line_percent
title: Line Chart with Percent axis
description: This example shows how to format the tick labels of the y-axis of a chart as percentages.

name: line_with_ci
title: Line Chart with Confidence Interval Band
description: How to make a line chart with a bootstrapped 95% confidence interval band.

name: line_with_last_value_labeled
title: Line Chart with Last Value Labeled
description: This chart shows a line chart with a label annotating the final value

name: line_with_log_scale
title: Line Chart with Logarithmic Scale
description: How to make a line chart on a `Logarithmic scale <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logarithmic_scale>`_.

name: london_tube
title: London Tube Lines
description:
This example shows the London tube lines against the background of the
borough boundaries. It is based on the vega-lite example at
https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/geo_layer_line_london.html.

name: maps_faceted_species
title: Faceted County-Level Choropleth Maps
description:
A set of maps arranged in a grid, each showing the distribution of a species' projected habitat across US counties.

Each choropleth map uses color intensity to represent the percentage values within county boundaries.

name: multi_series_line
title: Multiple Series Line Chart
description: This example shows how to make a line chart with multiple series of data.

name: multifeature_scatter_plot
title: Multifeature Scatter Plot
description: This example shows how to make a scatter plot with multiple feature encodings.

name: multiline_highlight
title: Multi-Line Highlight
description:
This multi-line chart uses an invisible Voronoi tessellation to handle pointerover to
identify the nearest point and then highlight the line on which the point falls.
It is adapted from the Vega-Lite example found at
https://bl.ocks.org/amitkaps/fe4238e716db53930b2f1a70d3401701

name: multiline_tooltip
title: Multi-Line Tooltip
description:
This example shows how you can use selections and layers to create a
tooltip-like behavior tied to the x position of the cursor.
If you are looking for more standard tooltips, see the :ref:`gallery_multiline_tooltip_standard` example.

In this example, we'll employ a little trick to isolate the x-position of the
cursor: we add some transparent points with only an x encoding (no y encoding)
and tie a *nearest* selection to these, tied to the "x" field.

name: multiline_tooltip_standard
title: Multi-Line Tooltip (Standard)
description:
This example shows how to add a standard tooltip to the same chart
as in :ref:`gallery_multiline_tooltip`. You can find another example
using this approach in the documentation on the :ref:`user-guide-pivot-transform` transformation.

name: multiple_interactions
title: Multiple Interactions
description:
This example shows how multiple user inputs can be layered onto a chart. The four inputs have functionality as follows:

* Dropdown: Filters the movies by genre
* Radio Buttons: Highlights certain films by Worldwide Gross
* Mouse Drag and Scroll: Zooms the x and y scales to allow for panning.

name: natural_disasters
title: Global Deaths from Natural Disasters
description: This example shows a proportional symbols visualization of deaths from natural disasters by year and type.

name: normalized_stacked_area_chart
title: Normalized Stacked Area Chart
description: This example shows how to make a normalized stacked area chart.

name: normalized_stacked_bar_chart
title: Normalized Stacked Bar Chart
description: This is an example of a normalized stacked bar chart using data which contains crop yields over different regions and different years in the 1930s.

name: normed_parallel_coordinates
title: Normalized Parallel Coordinates
description:
A `Parallel Coordinates <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_coordinates>`_
chart is a chart that lets you visualize the individual data points by drawing
a single line for each of them.

Such a chart can be created in Altair by first transforming the data into a
suitable representation.

This example shows a modified parallel coordinates chart with the Penguins dataset,
where the y-axis shows the value after min-max rather than the raw value. It's a
simplified Altair version of `the VegaLite version <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/parallel_coordinate.html>`_

name: one_dot_per_zipcode
title: One Dot Per Zipcode
description: This example shows a geographical plot with one dot per zipcode.

name: pacman_chart
title: Pacman Chart
description:
Chart made using ``mark_arc`` and constant values.
This could also be made using
``alt.Chart(source).mark_arc(color = "gold", theta = (5/8)*np.pi, theta2 = (19/8)*np.pi,radius=100)``.

name: parallel_coordinates
title: Parallel Coordinates
description:
A `Parallel Coordinates <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_coordinates>`_
chart is a chart that lets you visualize the individual data points by drawing
a single line for each of them.
Such a chart can be created in Altair by first transforming the data into a
suitable representation.
This example shows a parallel coordinates chart with the Penguins dataset.

name: percentage_of_total
title: Calculating Percentage of Total
description:
This chart demonstrates how to use a joinaggregate transform to display
data values as a percentage of total.

name: pie_chart
title: Pie Chart
description:
This example shows how to make a Pie Chart using ``mark_arc``.
This is adapted from a corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Pie Chart <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/arc_pie.html>`_.

name: pie_chart_with_labels
title: Pie Chart with Labels
description:
This example shows how to layer text over arc marks (``mark_arc``) to label pie charts.
This is adapted from a corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Pie Chart with Labels <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/layer_arc_label.html>`_.

name: point_map
title: Point map
description: This is a layered map that shows the positions of airports on a background of U.S. states.

name: polar_bar_chart
title: Polar Bar Chart
description:
This example shows how to make a polar bar chart using ``mark_arc``.
This could also have been called a "pie chart with axis labels",
but is more commonly referred to as a polar bar chart.
The axis lines are created using pie charts with only the stroke visible.

name: poly_fit_regression
title: Polynomial Fit Plot with Regression Transform
description:
This example shows how to overlay data with multiple fitted polynomials using
the regression transform.

name: pyramid
title: Pyramid Pie Chart
description: Altair reproduction of http://robslink.com/SAS/democd91/pyramid_pie.htm

name: radial_chart
title: Radial Chart
description:
This radial plot uses both angular and radial extent to convey multiple dimensions of data.
This is adapted from a corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Radial Plot <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/arc_radial.html>`_.

name: ranged_dot_plot
title: Ranged Dot Plot
description: This example shows a ranged dot plot to convey changing life expectancy for the five most populous countries (between 1955 and 2000).

name: ridgeline_plot
title: Ridgeline plot
description:
A `Ridgeline plot <https://serialmentor.com/blog/2017/9/15/goodbye-joyplots>`_
lets you visualize distribution of a numeric value for different
subsets of data (what we call "facets" in Altair).

Such a chart can be created in Altair by first transforming the data into a
suitable representation.

name: scatter_faceted
title: Faceted Scatter Plot
description: A series of scatter plots, one for each country/area of origin.

name: scatter_href
title: Scatter Plot with Href
description:
This example shows a scatter plot with an ``href`` encoding constructed from
the car name. With this encoding, you can click on any of the points to open
a google search for the car name.

name: scatter_linked_brush
title: Multi-panel Scatter Plot with Linked Brushing
description:
This is an example of using an interval selection to control the color of
points across multiple panels.

name: scatter_linked_table
title: Brushing Scatter Plot to Show Data on a Table
description:
A scatter plot of the cars dataset, with data tables for horsepower, MPG, and origin.
The tables update to reflect the selection on the scatter plot.

name: scatter_marginal_hist
title: Scatter Plot with Faceted Marginal Histograms
description:
This example demonstrates how to generate a scatter plot,
with faceted marginal histograms that share their respective x- and y-limits.

name: scatter_matrix
title: Scatter Matrix
description:
An example of using a RepeatChart to construct a multi-panel scatter plot
with linked panning and zooming.

name: scatter_point_paths_hover
title: Scatter plot with point paths on hover with search box
description:
This example combines cross-sectional analysis (comparing countries at a single point in time)
with longitudinal analysis (tracking changes in individual countries over time), using
an interactive visualization technique inspired by [this Vega example](https://vega.github.io/vega/examples/global-development/).

Key features:
1. Point Paths. On hover, shows data trajectories using a trail mark that
thickens from past to present, clearly indicating the direction of time.
2. Search Box. Implements a case-insensitive regex filter for country names,
enabling dynamic, flexible data point selection to enhance exploratory analysis.

name: scatter_qq
title: Quantile-Quantile Plot
description: A quantile-quantile plot comparing input data to theoretical distributions.

name: scatter_tooltips
title: Simple Scatter Plot with Tooltips
description:
A scatter plot of the cars dataset, with tooltips showing selected column
values when you hover over points. We make the points larger so that it is
easier to hover over them.

name: scatter_with_histogram
title: Scatter Plot and Histogram with Interval Selection
description:
This example shows how to link a scatter plot and a histogram
together such that an interval selection in the histogram will
plot the selected values in the scatter plot.

Note that both subplots need to know about the `mbin` field created
by the `transform_bin` method. In order to achieve this, the data is
not passed to the `Chart()` instances creating the subplots, but
directly in the `hconcat()` function, which joins the two plots together.

name: scatter_with_labels
title: Simple Scatter Plot with Labels
description: This example shows a basic scatter plot with labels created with Altair.

name: scatter_with_layered_histogram
title: Interactive Scatter Plot and Linked Layered Histogram
description:
This example shows how to link a scatter plot and a histogram
together such that clicking on a point in the scatter plot will
isolate the distribution corresponding to that point, and vice versa.

name: scatter_with_loess
title: Scatter Plot with LOESS Lines
description:
This example shows how to add a trend line to a scatter plot using
the LOESS transform (LOcally Estimated Scatter Plot Smoothing).

name: scatter_with_minimap
title: Scatter Plot with Minimap
description:
This example shows how to create a miniature version of a plot
such that creating a selection in the miniature version
adjusts the axis limits in another, more detailed view.

name: scatter_with_rolling_mean
title: Scatter Plot with Rolling Mean
description:
A scatter plot with a rolling mean overlay. In this example a 30 day window
is used to calculate the mean of the maximum temperature around each date.

name: scatter_with_shaded_area
title: Scatter Plot with Shaded Area
description:
This example shows a scatter plot with shaded area,
constructed using :ref:`area mark <user-guide-area-marks>` and :ref:`rect mark <user-guide-rect-marks>`.

name: seattle_weather_interactive
title: Seattle Weather Interactive
description:
This chart provides an interactive exploration of Seattle weather over the
course of the year. It includes a one-axis brush selection to easily
see the distribution of weather types in a particular date range.

name: select_detail
title: Selection Detail
description:
This example shows a selection that links two views of data: the left panel
contains one point per object, and the right panel contains one line per
object. Clicking on either the points or lines will select the corresponding
objects in both views of the data.

The challenge lies in expressing such hierarchical data in a way that Altair
can handle. We do this by merging the data into a "long form" dataframe, and
aggregating identical metadata for the final plot.

name: select_mark_area
title: Using Selection Interval with mark_area
description:
Because area is considered one object, just using the plain
selector will select the entire area instead of just one part of it.

This example shows how to use two areas, one on top of the other, and a
`transform_filter` to fake out this effect.

name: selection_histogram
title: Selection Histogram
description:
This chart shows an example of using an interval selection to filter the
contents of an attached histogram, allowing the user to see the proportion
of items in each category within the selection.

name: selection_layer_bar_month
title: Interactive Average
description:
The plot below uses an interval selection, which causes the chart to include an interactive brush
(shown in grey). The brush selection parameterizes the red guideline, which visualizes the average
value within the selected interval.

name: selection_zorder
title: Selection zorder
description:
This example shows how to bring selected points to the front/foreground
by using a condition to change the point's (z)order
as it is hovered over with the pointer.
This prevents that the selected points are obscured
by those that are not selected.

name: simple_bar_chart
title: Simple Bar Chart
description: This example shows a basic bar chart created with Altair.

name: simple_heatmap
title: Simple Heatmap
description: This example shows a simple heatmap for showing gridded data.

name: simple_histogram
title: Simple Histogram
description:
This example shows how to make a basic histogram, based on the vega-lite docs
https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/histogram.html

name: simple_line_chart
title: Simple Line Chart
description:
This chart shows the most basic line chart, made from a dataframe with two
columns.

name: simple_scatter_with_errorbars
title: Simple Scatter Plot with Errorbars
description: A simple scatter plot of a data set with errorbars.

name: simple_stacked_area_chart
title: Simple Stacked Area Chart
description: This example shows how to make a simple stacked area chart.

name: slider_cutoff
title: Slider Cutoff
description: This example shows how to bind a variable parameter to a slider, and how to use the corresponding bound value to color data points.  This example is based on an example from the Altair 4 documentation for Interactions, in which the  interactivity was accomplished using a selection.  The version below has been simplified significantly through the use of a variable parameter.  Variable parameters were added in Altair 5.

name: slope_graph
title: Slope Graph
description: This example shows how to make Slope Graph.

name: sorted_error_bars_with_ci
title: Sorted Error Bars showing Confidence Interval
description: This example shows how to show error bars using confidence intervals, while also sorting the y-axis based on x-axis values.

name: stacked_bar_chart
title: Stacked Bar Chart
description: This is an example of a stacked bar chart using data which contains crop yields over different regions and different years in the 1930s.

name: stacked_bar_chart_sorted_segments
title: Stacked Bar Chart with Sorted Segments
description: This is an example of a stacked-bar chart with the segments of each bar resorted.

name: stacked_bar_chart_with_text
title: Stacked Bar Chart with Text Overlay
description:
This example shows how to overlay text on a stacked bar chart. For both the
bar and text marks, we use the ``stack`` argument in the ``x`` encoding to
cause the values to be stacked horizontally.

name: stem_and_leaf
title: Stem and Leaf Plot
description: This example shows how to make a stem and leaf plot.

name: step_chart
title: Step Chart
description:
This example shows Google's stock price over time.
This uses the "step-after" interpolation scheme.
The full list of interpolation options includes 'linear',
'linear-closed', 'step', 'step-before', 'step-after', 'basis',
'basis-open', 'basis-closed', 'cardinal', 'cardinal-open',
'cardinal-closed', 'bundle', and 'monotone'.

name: streamgraph
title: Streamgraph
description: This example shows the streamgraph from vega-lite examples.

name: strip_plot
title: Simple Strip Plot
description: A simple example of how to make a strip plot.

name: strip_plot_jitter
title: Strip Plot with Jitter
description:
In this chart, we encode the ``Major Genre`` column from the ``movies`` dataset
in the ``y``-channel. In the default presentation of this data, it would be
difficult to gauge the relative frequencies with which different values occur
because there would be so much overlap. To address this, we use the ``yOffset``
channel to incorporate a random offset (jittering). The example is shown twice,
on the left side using normally distributed and on the right side using
uniformally distributed jitter.

name: table_bubble_plot_github
title: Table Bubble Plot (Github Punch Card)
description: This example shows github contributions by the day of week and hour of the day.

name: top_k_items
title: Top K Items
description:
This example shows how to use the window and transformation filter to display
the Top items of a long list of items in decreasing order.
Here we sort the top 10 highest ranking movies of IMDB.

name: top_k_letters
title: Top K Letters
description:
This example shows how to use a window transform in order to display only the
top K categories by number of entries. In this case, we rank the characters in
the first paragraph of Dickens' *A Tale of Two Cities* by number of occurrences.

name: top_k_with_others
title: Top-K Plot with Others
description:
This example shows how to use aggregate, window, and calculate transformations
to display the top-k directors by average worldwide gross while grouping the
remaining directors as 'All Others'.

name: trail_marker
title: Line Chart with Varying Size
description: This is example of using the ``trail`` marker to vary the size of a line.

name: us_employment
title: The U.S. Employment Crash During the Great Recession
description: This example is a fully developed bar chart with negative values using the sample dataset of U.S. employment changes during the Great Recession.

name: us_incomebrackets_by_state_facet
title: US Income by State: Wrapped Facet
description:
This example shows how to create a map of income in the US by state,
faceted over income brackets

name: us_population_over_time
title: US Population by Age and Sex
description:
This chart visualizes the age distribution of the US population over time.
It uses a slider widget that is bound to the year to visualize the age
distribution over time.

name: us_population_over_time_facet
title: US Population: Wrapped Facet
description:
This chart visualizes the age distribution of the US population over time,
using a wrapped faceting of the data by decade.

name: us_population_pyramid_over_time
title: US Population Pyramid Over Time
description:
A population pyramid shows the distribution of age groups within a population.
It uses a slider widget that is bound to the year to visualize the age
distribution over time.

name: us_state_capitals
title: U.S. State Capitals Overlaid on a Map of the U.S
description:
This is a layered geographic visualization that shows US capitals
overlaid on a map.

name: violin_plot
title: Violin Plot
description: This example shows how to make a Violin Plot using Altair's density transform.

name: waterfall_chart
title: Waterfall Chart
description:
This example shows how to recreate a Vega-Lite implementation of a waterfall chart.
Original inspiration is from https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/waterfall_chart.html

name: wheat_wages
title: Wheat and Wages
description:
A recreation of William Playfair's classic chart visualizing
the price of wheat, the wages of a mechanic, and the reigning British monarch.

This is a more polished version of the simpler chart in :ref:`gallery_bar_and_line_with_dual_axis`.

name: wilkinson-dot-plot
title: Wilkinson Dot Plot
description: An example of a `Wilkinson Dot Plot <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot_plot_(statistics)>`_

name: wind_vector_map
title: Wind Vector Map
description:
An example showing a vector array map showing wind speed and direction using ``wedge``
as shape for ``mark_point`` and ``angle`` encoding for the wind direction.
This is adapted from this corresponding Vega-Lite Example:
`Wind Vector Map <https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/examples/point_angle_windvector.html>`_
with an added base map.

name: window_rank
title: Window Rank Line Chart
description:
This example shows the Group F rankings in the 2018 World Cup after each matchday.
A window transformation is used to rank each after each match day, sorting by points and difference.

name: world_map
title: World Map
description:
This example shows how to create a world map using data generators for
different background layers.

name: world_projections
title: World Projections
description:
This example shows a map of the countries of the world.
Use the dropdown menu to compare projections. For more details on the `project` arguments, see the API of `altair.Projection <https://altair-viz.github.io/user_guide/generated/core/altair.Projection.html>`_.
